source.title: Ziya2: Data-centric Learning is All LLMs Need
source.authors: Ruyi Gan; Zi-Wei Wu; Renliang Sun; Junyu Lu; Xiaojun Wu; Di Zhang; Kun-Hao Pan; Jun-Qing He; Yuanhe Tian; Ping Yang; Qi Yang; Hao Wang; Jia-Xing Zhang; Yan Song

record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to data attributes during continual pre-training, and reports downstream benchmark performance across training checkpoints. It does not reproduce the original parameter/token/compute scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: Section 7 fits a data-attribute scaling relation to downstream-task test loss at fixed model size; this is not held-out pre-training loss or a compute-optimal allocation result. Figure 6 reports benchmark performance at training-token checkpoints. Those checkpoint results are recorded for V6; values shown only in the figure are marked figure only.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power-law loss relation in a new training regime: fixed-size continual pre-training with data-quality-adjusted token volume (V5). Its downstream test-loss fit and benchmark trajectories also bear on V6, although it does not validate out-of-sample prediction. The record incorrectly excludes the Section 7 fit from all versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that semantic and grammatical data quality are more effective than task-specific augmentation when general-task performance is considered, and recommend mixing augmented data with high-quality generic data while reporting general-task results. Their broader conclusion is that the three-stage data-centric continual-pre-training approach improves Ziya2 over LLaMA2. The relative importance of data attributes is inferred from their fitted coefficients.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a fixed-size model and fits downstream-task test loss to an adjusted data-volume term incorporating Coherence, Readability, and Similarity. It does not use the original parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted relation incorporates the selected data attributes and uses the stated Huber-loss/L-BFGS fitting procedure; alternative attributes or fitting choices are not compared.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted coefficients for coherence and readability exceed the similarity coefficient, motivating the authors' data-quality recommendations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this fitted continual-pre-training model, semantic and grammatical data quality have larger effective-volume weights than similarity to downstream tests.

record.problems: The data-centric fit uses 84 samples at a fixed model size; the text reports no uncertainty estimates or alternative-fit comparisons. Figure 6 checkpoint values are presented only graphically.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling over several orders of magnitude in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of runs orders of magnitude larger from fits on small runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its stability across compute budgets.
Loss sensitivity to architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, other model sizes, repeated-data scaling, and generality beyond this fixed-size continual-pre-training experiment; predictive validation of the fitted power-law form.
Out-of-sample prediction of downstream performance, parameter scaling, and downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss. Benchmark accuracy is not fitted to a predictive scaling relation.
Comparisons of fitted exponents or optimal allocations across setups or fitting choices, disagreements between published laws, and demonstrated departures from a single fitted loss power law.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Figure 6's numerical labels and Table 3 make most purportedly figure-only values available. Row states describe local training-volume changes, with initialization used for the first checkpoint; recovery that remains below initialization is marked partial. These descriptive score changes do not independently establish predictive accuracy. Section 7 uses separate, unmixed stage datasets, unlike the sequential mixed-data training in Section 6.3; the two experiments must remain distinct. No uncertainty or fit-quality statistic is reported. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pre-training loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits on small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Whether the original power-law form holds across modalities or other training regimes.
The study plots downstream benchmark performance against training tokens but does not fit or assess a quantitative predictive relationship, or relate benchmark performance to pre-training loss.
It uses one stated fitting procedure and does not compare exponents or compute-optimal allocations across fitting choices or setups.

rows.subject: Ziya2-13B fixed-size continual-pre-training experiments
rows.stage_stated: Continual pre-training; data from the three stages is used separately
rows.operation_detail: Fit the reported loss relation against adjusted data volume.
rows.measure: Downstream-task test loss as a function of adjusted data volume D
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.note: A fixed-model-size data-centric loss fit, not held-out pre-training loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
rows.check: The fitted relation L(D)=D^-0.06+0.31 bears on power-law loss in continual pre-training and downstream test-loss scaling. It is an in-sample fit to 84 observations, with no reported fit error, uncertainty, or held-out prediction test; it is not V1 held-out pretraining loss.
